title: coordinated-mini-saga-for-canary-snapshots
author: Aisha Kapoor
release_notes: Adds coordinated mini-saga mechanism for creating consistent canary snapshots across services to enable atomic rollback and replay, plus operator runbook and integration tests.
description: Motivation: During multi-service canaries we observed inconsistent snapshots and partial rollbacks that left sessions or KV caches in incompatible states. This PR introduces a lightweight coordinated "mini-saga" mechanism that captures consistent snapshot points across participating services, exposes a promote/rollback API, and wires the controller into existing rollout orchestration so canary promote/rollback becomes atomic at the snapshot granularity. Changes include a new saga coordinator in the rollout controller, snapshot versioning and tombstone markers for rollbacks, a dry-run promote mode for rehearsal, and operator runbook + docs. Checklist: 1) Implement saga coordinator and snapshot protocol (controller + runtime hooks) 2) Add snapshot lifecycle API and RBAC entries 3) Add integration tests for cross-service snapshot capture and rollback 4) Add runbook and example playbook for SREs 5) Validate with canary scenarios and perf microbenchmarks. Impact: small runtime hook added to RuntimeKV and SessionManager to fence snapshots; controller implements two-phase commit-like flow with timeout-based compensating actions. Backwards compatibility: non-participating services ignore saga headers; rollout controller falls back to previous behavior when saga enrollment fails. How to validate: unit + integration tests included, manual steps in docs to simulate race conditions, and a dry-run promote that records but does not switch traffic. Rollout plan: feature gated behind rollout.feature_flags.mini_saga and enabled on dedicated clusters first. Related: ENG-4521 (cross-service rollback incidents), ENG-4672 (session-coherence perf study).

Monica: Requested RBAC review and docs clarity for SRE playbook, asked to gate feature flag by default. risk_assessment: medium: introduces coordinated state across services but is opt-in and feature-flagged; compensating logic exists for partial failures; integration tests added to cover common races. Monitor: rollout.snapshot.latency, rollout.snapshot.failures, session.reconcile.errors.
notes: Operator runbook includes a step to replay snapshots in read-only dry-run mode and to escalate to manual rollback if compensating actions are unsuccessful. The dry-run promote is recommended for first 48 hours post-merge in controlled clusters.
